item.text: I’ve got enough: the evidence is strongly one-sided, with only one or two narrow technocratic counterexamples. I’m writing the compact note now and will keep it to claim-level items only.

**Verdict:** No.

Putin did not meaningfully resist corruption, favoritism, monopolies, oligarchic capture, or politically connected business privilege in 2023. The clearest evidence points the other way: pressure on business elites, discriminatory treatment of foreign investors, and state takeovers of assets. The only counterevidence is narrow, technocratic restraint from Nabiullina and other economic officials.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Putin tells Russia's billionaires to put patriotism before profit | Reuters | 16 Mar 2023 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/putin-urges-russias-billionaires-to-invest-in-face-of-sanctions-war-3032372) | Strong negative evidence: Putin told business elites their role was to support society and the state, not just make money. That is loyalty extraction from oligarchic and connected business, not a clean anti-capture posture. | 5B.5; also 5B.1, 5B.4, 5B.2 |
| Putin signs law on barring 'unfriendly' foreigners from owning stakes in Russian firms - RIA | Reuters | 8 Apr 2023 | [link](https://uk.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-signs-law-on-barring-unfriendly-foreigners-from-owning-stakes-in-russian-firms--ria-3112093) | Putin backed a law allowing Russia to bar “unfriendly” foreigners from stakes in major firms and banks and potentially redistribute those shares. That is favoritism and politicized control, not neutral competition. | 5B.5; also 5B.4, 5B.3 |
| Putin signs decree taking over Russian assets of two foreign firms | Reuters | 25 Apr 2023 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-signs-decree-taking-over-russian-assets-of-two-foreign-firms-3064283) | Direct evidence against clean governance: Putin created temporary state control over Russian assets of two foreign energy firms. This signals arbitrary expropriation risk and political favoritism, not anti-corruption discipline. | 5B.5; also 5B.4, 5B.3 |
| Russia's 2024 defense spending rise record share of budget | Reuters | 29 Sep 2023 | [link](https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russias-2024-defense-spending-rise-record-share-budget-2023-09-29/) | Defense spending absorbing about a third of the budget reinforces elite-linked war priorities over broad civilian development. It is not corruption proof by itself, but it undercuts the idea of neutral, public-interest economic governance. | 5B.5; also 5B.1, 5B.3 |
| Russia should not take temporary control of foreign banks' units - central bank | Reuters | 28 Apr 2023 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/russia-should-not-take-temporary-control-of-foreign-banks-units-central-bank-3067714) | Narrow counterevidence: Nabiullina opposed a more arbitrary seizure of foreign bank units, suggesting some rule-based restraint inside the system. This is a technocratic check, not proof that Putin himself resisted oligarchic privilege or corruption. | 5B.5; also 5B.2, 5B.3, 5B.4 |
| Russian officials seek to streamline budget spending, but disagree on tax hikes | Reuters | 15 Jun 2023 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/russian-officials-seek-to-streamline-budget-spending-but-disagree-on-tax-hikes-3106392) | Technocrats including Siluanov, Reshetnikov, Oreshkin, and Nabiullina argued that higher taxes would hurt investment and growth. This shows some professional resistance to predatory fiscal choices, but only within a regime still driven by war spending and political control. | 5B.5; also 5B.2, 5B.3, 5B.4 |
| Russia: Freedom in the World 2023 | Freedom House | 2023 | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2023) | Broad background evidence: state power and private property are tightly intertwined in Russia, with officials using their positions to amass property and the state imposing takeovers and large tax penalties on selected firms after dubious proceedings. This is a systemic description of politicized property and capture, not anti-corruption reform. | 5B.5; also 5B.4, 5B.3, 5B.2 |

**Search gap:** I did not find credible evidence that Putin in 2023 launched or sustained a serious anti-corruption, anti-monopoly, or anti-oligarch capture campaign. The strongest pro-side material is limited to technocrats resisting arbitrary seizures and warning against harmful fiscal choices. The overall pattern is still loyalty-based control, selective expropriation, and politicized business privilege.
